title: envelope/safety.json — the ceilings, written by a person (2.1 rule 7, 10.3 rule 4)
description: Not a card and not knowledge: policy. A person writes it after confirming the limits outside the system, no agent may edit it (Tier 3), and nothing in it is transferred from anywhere else -- a safety limit written for another setup is reference material, not grounds. This schema exists because the file would otherwise be invisible: a JSON object with neither `card` nor `artifact` is skipped by the collector, so a mistyped key would leave check_budget returning `unavailable`, every run falling to Tier 2, and nothing reporting an error. The same silence held run logs until run_log.schema.json. The shape here is not invented: it is what simulation_agent/src/operator.py and axis_a5_budget.py already read.

policy_version.description: Recorded into every run log as safety_policy_version. Policy changes, so a run has to say which one it ran under; raise this whenever a ceiling moves, or the record cannot be read back.

written_by.description: The person who confirmed these limits. Not machine-read, and kept anyway: P0 rule 7 makes the confirmation the point, and a policy nobody signed is a preference.

basis.description: What the ceilings were chosen against -- which machine, what else it has to keep doing. A number without this cannot be revisited, only replaced.

targets.description: One row per place a run may execute. A second target is a data change here and not a code change: the cost model picks the smallest target that fits, and `intent` on the goal card decides between those that do (4.5.1). The target is deliberately not a capabilities/ configuration -- local and cluster run the same model and produce the same observable.

limit.description: A ceiling. value and unit only: this is a decision, not a measurement, so it carries no source and no grade -- P2's four parts describe a claim about the world, and a policy is not one.

unit.description: must be in units.json with a fixed SI factor, or si() refuses it

target.description: the id the operator is invoked with; `local` is its default

smoke_budget.description: Separate on purpose. A smoke run allowed the full budget tells you nothing before the run it precedes, and its second job is to replace the estimated cost-per-step with one measured on this machine -- so the budget comparison for the full run stops resting on an E5.
